description: service.json validation corpus: one directory of fixture manifests plus the accept/reject decision every validator must make for each, and the rule table both languages' validators share (#4858). See README.md for the runner matrix and the divergence legend.

implementations.discovery: runtime/discovery/validation.star validate(manifest) -> issue strings; accept means an empty list
implementations.discoveryManifest: runtime/discovery/manifest/validation.star validate_manifest(manifest) - a shim over the same validator since #4858
implementations.engine: runtime/engine/topologies/tilt/manifest/validator.star ManifestValidator.validate(manifest).valid. Recorded only where it returns a verdict: it crashes (Starlark type errors) on some wrongly-typed fields instead of rejecting, so 'engine' is absent for those fixtures.
implementations.cli: cli/src/utils/service-manifest.ts validateServiceManifest(manifest) - accept means no errors

expect.note: a command service runs as a local process - the schema and the CLI exempt it from stack/port; the discovery validators predate command services and still require stack and port; the engine requires port unconditionally
a database resource has no port; the engine's port is required unconditionally, so it rejects a manifest the schema explicitly allows
the engine validator crashes indexing a non-string appName - no verdict recorded
the CLI's docker-name check has no minimum length; the 2-character floor lives in the schema and the Starlark validators
schema and engine require a leading letter (^[a-z]); discovery only checks the character set, the CLI only checks Docker-name safety
the engine's hand-rolled pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ allows a trailing hyphen that the schema's ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]$ rejects

appName-too-long.note: 65 characters: every bound rejects it, though they disagree on the maximum (schema/discovery 64, CLI docker-name 59, engine 50)

expect.note: the engine's VALID_APP_TYPES list predates the agent resource type; the schema enum and the CLI accept it
infra is the engine's internal resource type: the Starlark validators know it, the published schema and the CLI do not
schemaVersion is required by the schema and the CLI; the Starlark validators never look at it
the CLI's validateServiceManifest checks port only when present; the schema's backend conditional (port required, 4000-5999) is enforced by the Ajv step, not this function
same shape-only contract as missing-port-backend: the schema requires port for bring-your-own, this function does not
the engine validator crashes comparing a string port to 1024 - no verdict recorded
below the 3000 floor. The CLI checks only the shared 1-65535 bound; the engine only warns when a port lands outside its band
inside the generic 3000-9999 window but outside the backend band (4000-5999). The engine only warns on band misses; the CLI never checks bands here
inside the generic window, outside the backend band - same split as port-3000
above the 9999 ceiling, still inside the CLI's 1-65535 shape check and the engine's 1024-65535 basic range
an imported Compose app keeps the port its own container listens on (#4637); the engine still rejects ports under 1024 before it looks at the appType
discovery whitelists feature names; the schema uses an enum; the CLI checks only that the entries are strings and the engine never checks item values
drizzle is a real schema feature the discovery whitelist never caught up with - drift in the strict direction
vite-node is in the discovery whitelist but missing from the schema enum - drift in the permissive direction
the CLI's dependsOnErrors skips non-arrays, so a string dependsOn is silently kept
the shared bound is 1-10; the engine's own VALIDATION_THRESHOLDS caps at 5
the engine validator crashes comparing a string replicas to 1 - no verdict recorded
the CLI refuses replicas > 1 on a frontend (Compose generates one container); the other validators do not make that distinction
the schema requires featuresEnabled on a worker; nothing else does
